seoTitle: Everything you need to know about moving with your pet
seoDesc: Discover all our practical tips for preparing your pet as well as possible for a move.
h1: How do you prepare your pet for a move?

intro.p: For us, moving house is an exciting fresh start. For our pets, their whole world is turned upside down. Dogs, cats, rabbits and birds all feel these changes deeply. Fortunately, a few simple precautions can turn this ordeal into a smooth transition for the whole family.

body.p: Animals are creatures of habit who build their own territorial landmarks. The unusual commotion, the piling boxes and the constant comings and goings disrupt their reassuring routine.
Some animals become anxious, others hide or lose their appetite. Recognising these signs of stress lets you adapt your approach.

sections.h: Preparing your pet before the big day

body.p: Planning ahead is your best ally. Start by gradually getting your pet used to its carrier if it is not already. Keep its usual routine as far as possible: the same mealtimes, the same walks, the same games. This stability amid the surrounding chaos reassures it enormously.
Also think about the practical side:

ul: Update its vaccinations and have its health record ready
Order enough food to avoid a sudden change of diet
Clearly identify your pet with a tag showing your new contact details
Prepare a first-aid kit with its usual medication

body.p: This hectic day requires special arrangements for your companion. Ideally, leave it with a relative or at a pet boarding facility for the day. If that is not possible, keep it in a quiet room with its belongings, fresh water and favourite toys. Put a sign on the door so that nobody opens it by mistake.

sections.h: The journey to the new home

body.p: During the journey, keep your pet in a suitable, secure carrier. Dogs can travel with their harness attached to the seat belt. Plan regular breaks on long journeys and never leave your pet alone in the vehicle, especially in hot weather.
On arrival, first set up a refuge room with familiar items: bed, bowls, toys and a litter tray for cats. Let it explore the other spaces gradually, at its own pace.
Don't worry if it hides or seems disoriented in the first few days: this is a normal reaction while it rebuilds its bearings.
Patience and kindness should accompany this transition period. Some animals adapt in a few hours, others need several weeks. Keep a stable routine and give it plenty of attention.
For dogs, regular walks are an excellent way to discover the new neighbourhood and feel at ease there.

sections.h: A move designed for the whole family

body.p: Your pet is an integral part of your family and deserves all our attention. At Gérard & Fils, we adapt our work to minimise its stress: flexible hours, quiet areas kept undisturbed and careful handling of its belongings.
Because a successful move is one where everyone arrives happily in their new home, including the four-legged members!
